name: Support Services Building
summary: A buff-brick office complex stepping up the slope, presenting four regular storeys to the lower drive and three storeys with tall square piers along Western Road, backed by a low service wing and two rooftop mechanical penthouses.

evidence.note: Four exposed rows, six bays on the left of the glazed stair strip. Warm buff brick samples #9c897b and #9b8973. Reflection in the lower glass sampled #5d7e77.
Six tall openings across the upper north end and a glazed vertical return.
Three rows above the upper lawn. Broad, mullioned openings within a square masonry frame face the intersection.
Street elevation shows the recessed ground level between masonry posts.
Flat roofs at several levels, a low angled service wing beside the loading apron and two main equipment enclosures.

P50 20.9 m, P90 28.31 m, maximum 33.74 m above inventory ground. Lower drive block is near 22 m, the link 18 m, roadside block 27 m, and service wing 6 m. The Eastern sidewalk stands about 13 m above the low yard.

Six taller windows before the stair strip and six beyond. Four complete rows above the guardrail with part of a fifth below it. The staircase has dark vertical glass strips either side of a ribbed pale metal panel.
The west roof DSM shows an approximately 26.6 m plant plateau along the east side, with a westward shoulder and a separate lower cap to its south.

parts.name: Low east return of service wing
Western Road block below upper spandrel
Western Road upper offices above recessed frontage

notes: The roadside grade hides the lowest floors. The lower-drive wall has a narrow vertical stair window between wider brick panels. The service entrance and hidden yard openings are approximate. Western Road grade meets the arcade roughly three storeys above the lower-drive datum. Lidar at (-145,47) and (-153,50) reads 26.5 and 26.6 m.
